text.p: British Airways said on Friday that it was disappointed by USAir Group Inc's decision to cancel a key marketing alliance between the two carriers -- a move that pushed their three-year partnership nearer to collapse.
"This is a disappointing decision, bearing in mind the great benefits that BA has brought to USAir," a BA spokesman said early on Friday.
"We remain convinced of the view that a continued alliance between BA and USAir is in the interests of both airlines, their customers, employees and shareholders," he added.
"We will ensure that customers are given equal or greater benefits as a result of future endeavours," the spokesman added.
USAir, in which BA has a 24.6 percent stake, said on Thursday that it would end its code-sharing pact and frequent flier programmes with BA on March 29 next year.
Relations between BA and USAir have turned increasingly sour since BA announced plans to form a massive alliance with powerhouse AMR, parent of American Airlines.
USAir has sued the two carriers and contended that their planned pact would undermine its own partnership with BA.
BA said that it planned to work with USAir until the code-sharing pact was ended next year and that services should not be affected.
